note: Wilkins as first translator of the Bhagavad Gita: primary chapter HIS-20. Charles Wilkins is not mentioned in any source fetched for this chapter (NCERT hess206 covers Jones, Colebrooke and Halhed only), so the fact is not taught here.

Pitt's India Act passed in August 1784 (IGNOU Block 6, Unit 23: 'Pitt's India Act was passed in August, 1784'). Primary HIS-27, but squarely in this chapter's acts_policies scope; taught in section 'acts' with practice q01.

Persian replaced by English as official language, 1835. Taught by combining two fetched sources: NCERT hess206 (English Education Act of 1835 made English the medium of instruction for higher education) and IGNOU BHIC-134 Unit 4 (Persian was the language of official records). Taught in section 'education'.

Bank key names Warren Hastings, flagged doubtful_key in the bank, and it conflicts with WBCS-2016-Q32 (key: Cornwallis) and with IGNOU Block 6 Unit 24, which credits Cornwallis with organising the civil service from 1793. The chapter discloses this conflict in the 'administration' section and an exam_note, but the doubtful key itself is not taught as fact.

Dalhousie introduced railways and telegraphs: primary chapter HIS-16. Fetched sources confirm Dalhousie created all-India Post and Telegraph departments (IGNOU BHIC-134 Unit 4) and the colonial purpose of railways (IGNOU Unit 9), but do not state that he introduced the railways; not taught here.
'Taccavi' (loans to peasants): no fetched authorised source (NCERT / IGNOU / NIOS / e-PG Pathshala) defines the term taccavi, so it is not taught in this chapter.

Indian Civil Service introduced under Lord Cornwallis (IGNOU Block 6 Unit 24: administrative structure 'started taking shape from 1793 under Cornwallis'; he reformed the service, banned private trade, raised salaries). Taught in section 'administration' with practice q17.

'Drain of Wealth' — Dadabhai Naoroji (IGNOU Unit 9: Naoroji is 'the major proponent and propagator of the drain of wealth'). Taught in section 'drain' with practice q08; the section's deep text notes that no book of the exact title 'Drain of Wealth' exists — Naoroji's book is Poverty and Un-British Rule in India (1901).
First railway line 1853, Bombay–Thane: this fact appears in none of the fetched authorised sources (it was found only on coaching sites, which are not permitted sources); not taught in this chapter.

Dalhousie advocateded rapid railway construction: primary chapter HIS-16. Same railway-source gap as WBCS-2015-Q58 — fetched sources cover Dalhousie's Post/Telegraph departments but not his railway policy; not taught here.

Asiatic Society of Bengal founded by Sir William Jones (NCERT hess206: Jones 'set up the Asiatic Society of Bengal'). Primary HIS-20, but in this chapter's education-policy scope; taught in section 'education' with practice q10.
Poverty and Un-British Rule in India — Dadabhai Naoroji, 1901 (IGNOU Unit 9). Taught in section 'drain' with practice q09.
Drain Theory put forward by Dadabhai Naoroji (IGNOU Unit 9). Taught in section 'drain' with practice q08.

Bank key dates the first cotton textile mill to 1818, but the fetched IGNOU BHIC-134 Unit 8 states the first Indian mill was set up in Bombay in 1854. The conflict is disclosed in the chapter's exam_focus, but the bank key is not taught as fact.

Governor-General of Bengal when the Asiatic Society was founded — Warren Hastings. Supported by NCERT hess202 (Hastings Governor-General 1773–1785) and hess206 (Jones arrived 1783, set up the Society; Hastings an enthusiastic Orientalist supporter). Primary HIS-20; taught in section 'education'.

Ryotwari settlement in Madras — Thomas Munro (NCERT hess203: ryotwari 'subsequently developed by Thomas Munro'; IGNOU Unit 6: Munro appointed Governor of Madras 1820). Taught in section 'settlements' with practice q05.
Drain of Wealth theory — Dadabhai Naoroji (IGNOU Unit 9). Taught in section 'drain' with practice q08.
Bengal Tenancy Act passed in 1885 (IGNOU Unit 5: 'the government passed the Bengal Tenancy Act in 1885'). Taught in section 'countryside' with practice q31 and event ev08.

University of Calcutta established 1857 (NCERT hess206: 'In 1857... universities were being established in Calcutta, Madras and Bombay'). Primary HIS-20; taught in section 'education' with practice q35.
